# Floorplan
**See how your app actually fits together.**
Claude or Codex reads your codebase and draws an interactive map of it. Every part, file and web request gets a plain-English name, and every connection between them is shown.
[ ](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview)
[ ](docs/codex.md)
[ ](https://github.com/haydenschmitty/floorplan/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[ ](CHANGELOG.md)
[ ](LICENSE)
[ ](https://nodejs.org)
[ ](#how-it-works)
**[Try the live demo](https://haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo/)** · [Watch the video](https://youtu.be/NTUUzC7L_NQ) · [Install](#install) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Compared](#floorplan-archify-or-understand-anything) · [Features](#features) · [See it in action](#see-it-in-action) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [FAQ](#faq)
  ▶  Watch the walkthrough : installing Floorplan, then a tour of Brewline, a demo coffee-subscription app built across four repos.  
   Try the live demo →   Explore the Brewline map in your browser, no install needed. 
## Why Floorplan?
You built an app, probably with a lot of help from AI, and it works. But ask "what happens when someone checks out?" or "what breaks if I change this?" and the honest answer is *no idea*.
Floorplan gives you the diagram nobody drew. Ask Claude Code or Codex for a floorplan and a few minutes later you have a map you can explore, ask questions on, and keep up to date as you work.
- **For builders:** understand the app you made, in your own words, without reading the code.
- **For teams:** onboard someone in minutes, from the big picture down to the exact file.
- **For working with AI:** after every change Claude or Codex makes, see exactly which parts it touched and why.
## Floorplan, Archify or Understand Anything?
All three turn code into something you can see, and all three are worth knowing. They answer different questions:
| | **Floorplan** | **[Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)** | **[Understand Anything](https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The question it answers** | How does the app I built actually work, and what should I worry about? | How do I show this clearly? | How does this big codebase work, down to the functions? |
| **Made for** | People who build with AI and don't read the code | Anyone explaining a system, a process or an idea | Developers getting to know a large codebase |
| **What you get** | A zoomable map of your whole app: parts, files and endpoints,

itens.readme:
Pinky 
  Let AI use your iPhone or Android phone, with you in the loop: any agent from macOS, Windows or Linux, or Pinky itself, right on the phone.  
  Download  ·  Get started  ·  FAQ  ·  Discord  
 English ·  简体中文  ·  日本語  ·  Türkçe  
    A real Claude Code run on an Android 16 emulator. Pinky asks before payments by default; this run also asks before messages.  
Pinky lets any agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor or a script) operate a real iPhone or Android phone over MCP, while you watch on your computer, approve risky steps, take over and review what happened. Pinky can also do tasks by itself, with an AI model you choose: from your computer, or in Pinky's app right on the phone, with no computer at all. Whoever does the task, approvals are enforced by Pinky's gateway, not by instructions to the agent.
- **Every platform.** One app for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux. It drives Android phones (Android 10 to 17) and iPhones on iOS 17.4 or later: nothing to install on iOS 27 and later, and Pinky on the iPhone, Pinky's app, installed once from a Mac with Xcode on iOS 17.4 to 26, which you can also choose on iOS 27 (tried there, on a phone below it and on Simulators; [details](#phones)).
- **Tiny and native.** The window is drawn by [MyGo](https://github.com/egoist/mygo) on the GPU, with no Electron and no webview: a 16–22 MB download that idles at about 70 MB of memory and 0% CPU on a Mac.
- **Any agent, one click.** Settings › Agents connects Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor and more, and any agent that can use MCP servers works, on the same computer or over HTTP.
- **Pinky on the phone, no computer needed.** Pinky's app on Android and iPhone does tasks by itself with a model you choose, from DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi and GLM to Claude, GPT, Gemini and local models in Ollama or LM Studio. Type or speak a task, or share something to it; on Android, ask about what the screen shows from a floating button, and let it work on a hidden background screen while you keep using the phone ([how](#pinky-on-the-phone)).
- **Scheduled tasks and memory.** Pinky can run a task at set times or tell you when a condition holds, on the computer and on Android. After a task it may suggest a note to remember, such as a preference you told it, and keeps it only if you say yes ([more](#ask-pinky)).

itens.descricao_en: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
itens.readme:
# TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents
  Aaron J. Li 1 ,
  Weijia Xu 2 ,
  Chandan Singh 2 ,
  Zixiao Chen 3 ,
  Jeevana Priya Inala 2 ,
  Charlotte Siska 3 ,
  Acar Tamersoy 3 ,
  Bin Yu 1 ,
  Ion Stoica 1 ,
  Michel Galley 2 ,
  Jianfeng Gao 2 
   1 UC Berkeley    2 Microsoft Research    3 Microsoft Security
  Our measurement on SWE-Bench tasks:  18.4–30.9% lower mean cost  across five agent–model
  combinations, cheaper in  all 30  repository × combination cells, and Pass@1 up in
   4 of 5 .  Results 
TokenEconomizer makes coding agents cheaper to run in the repositories you work in often,
without changing the agent itself. It learns from the sessions an agent has already run in a
repository, and uses that experience to cut waste in the sessions that follow. It has three
mechanisms:
- **Micro-skills: remember how the repository works.** Sessions keep rediscovering the same
  facts: a build step that must run first, the spelling of a command that works here
  (`python -m pytest` where `pytest` is missing, `npx tsc` where `tsc` is), an environment
  variable a command needs, where generated files live. Micro-skills learns such facts, in any
  language, from two sources: failures that repeat across sessions, and a model that reviews the
  recent sessions every *k* sessions (*k* = 3) and proposes facts. A fact is stated at the start
  of each session once three sessions have confirmed it, and dropped when later sessions
  contradict it.
- **Tool pruning: stop loading tools that go unused.** Every loaded tool's definition is sent with
  every request. A tool that goes unused over *p* prompts spread across at least *m* sessions, or
  over *s* sessions of any length (*p* = 10, *m* = 2, *s* = 5), is left out of the next sessions
  through the agent's own settings. One command brings it back.
- **Failure-loop intervention (the loop guard): step in when a turn is stuck.** When a turn (the
  agent's work on one prompt) keeps hitting the same failures, a judge model checks whether it is
  stuck. If the judge is at least *c* sure (*c* = 0.7), the agent gets a redirect (a short note,
  added to its context, to try another approach), at most *r* times per turn (*r* = 1). If the
  turn is still stuck after that, TokenEconomizer tells you how to stop it; it never stops a turn
  itself.
TokenEconomizer is a plugin for **Claude Code**, **Codex**, the **GitHub Copilot CLI** and **Pi**,
with experimental support for **opencod

### About
OpenFilm turns any coding agent into a video agent, with editors to change anything it makes.
You and the agent work on the same film, together and live. Whatever the agent changes, you see as it happens; whatever
you change, the agent sees too. The agent does most of the work; you point at anything and ask for a change, or make it
yourself.
- **The agent makes the film.** Use Claude Code, Codex, any other coding agent, or the one built into the desktop
  app. It finds footage, music and voices, writes each shot and cuts them together while you watch.
- **Point at anything.** A clip, a moment, a stretch of the timeline, a spot in the frame, a line of subtitles, a card
  on the canvas. Point at it, say what you want, and the agent knows exactly what you mean.
- **Change it by hand.** Inside any shot, move, scale and rotate any element, retype its text, restyle its color, font
  and size, and animate it, even word by word. On the timeline, trim, split and reorder clips, change their speed,
  volume and fades, crop, grade and cut out the background, and edit subtitles and voice-over. Your edits land in the
  same files, and the agent builds on them.
### Installation
**Desktop app.** [Download it for macOS or Windows](https://github.com/openfilm/openfilm/releases/latest). Everything
you need comes with it, down to a built-in agent, and it works with Claude Code or Codex if you already use them.
**Your own coding agent.** Add the skill (needs Node 22.2+ and ffmpeg), then ask for a film:
```bash
npx skills add openfilm/openfilm
```
> Make a 20-second launch video for my CLI, with music.
### Editors
Each editor is a different way to work on the same film, and in every one you and the agent work together. OpenFilm
comes with four, and more official editors are in development for different kinds of people: simple enough for anyone
to pick up, and professional workbenches for those who want them. Editors follow the Community's open standard, so
anyone can build one and share it.

# huashu-art-motion · 艺术动画
让你的coding agent，把艺术风格写成会动的画。
36种艺术风格 · 9种解说语法 · 8种参数化片段 · 口播整片参考代码
```sh
npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion
```
[看动画](#动画样片) · [看风格](#看效果) · [开始使用](#里面有什么) · [下载完整样片](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest)
## 动态
- 2026-10：[Open Design](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design)（nexu-io 出品的开源 AI 设计工作区）的 [motion-design skill](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/blob/main/skills/motion-design/SOURCES.md) 把 huashu-art-motion 列为设计来源之一，并在 [skills/huashu-art-motion](https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/tree/main/skills/huashu-art-motion) 收录了一份适配版，保留了 MIT 许可和上游出处。很高兴这套艺术动画的做法被另一个开源项目用起来，谢谢 Open Design 团队。也欢迎更多项目使用、反馈和贡献。
## 动画样片
### 核心案例：花叔闯进超级玛丽
把自己做成像素主角，跑完一整关。砖块、水管、关卡运动与转场用代码完成，人物用生成帧合成；下面直接截自65秒成片。
连吃蘑菇都得先选会员：OpenAI，还是Claude？选完Claude，星芒道具落下来，花叔变大。
   连踩带踢 · 像素Sam与Dario客串敌人 
   钻进水管 · 金币密室与扫描线甩镜 
这组展示的是成片效果；GIF无声、循环播放。[片段时间点与导出参数](assets/showcase/mario-clips.md)。
### Clawd 博物馆奇妙夜
Claude Code 的像素吉祥物 Clawd 从保安电脑的终端里蹦出来，打着手电夜巡纽约大都会博物馆，再穿过中央公园去自然史博物馆，天亮前赶回来装成展品。98秒，16个场景，无口播，配乐也是代码合成的。
跳进梵高《麦田与柏树》：笔触方向取自原作的结构张量，Clawd被重画成厚涂。
   霸王龙骨架 · 追手电光斑 
   天亮 · 装成展品眨一下眼 
暗处是炭笔夜景，只有手电照到的地方显出颜色；入画的五幅（梵高、修拉、维米尔、伦勃朗、勒茨）都是大都会开放获取的CC0原作，按各自画家的笔法用代码重画。完整成片在[Releases](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest)，[片段时间点与说明](assets/showcase/clawd-clips.md)。
### 花叔穿越名画
画里真的会动。下面三段来自同一支穿越短片，场景用代码画，角色用生成帧合成。
日本桥上的一次水漂。
   古埃及 · 圣甲虫 
   8-bit · 顶出金币 
## 看效果
35段样片各取一帧：同一位少女、同一只橘白猫、同一张桌子，从公元前 40000 年的岩洞一路穿到 2026 年。每一段都在动：梵高的星空在转，马赛克的颜色从石块上流过去，水墨晕染把画面带进下一个时代。
注意：这 35 格用的是同一个构图，那是艺术史速通片的机制（风格在变、场景不变），不是这些风格的构图。做新题材要为题材重新构图，别把这间屋搬过去。
👉 [下载全风格样片（MP4）](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion/releases/latest)
长卷穿越片：一个人从左走到右，跨过边界的那一刻，世界和他自己的画风一起换（下图是收进仓库的 3 段示范：埃及壁画 → 莫奈《日本桥》→ 8-bit）：
8种解说语法各有一支可运行示范片（下图每镜取一帧）。此外还有第9种「讲解员式财经科普」，提供语法卡和需自备角色的整片代码快照。白板适合跟着口播画关系，Vox适合图形与信息拼贴：
| | |
|---|---|
|   Kurzgesagt：扁平无描边、尺度穿行 |   Vox：剪报、红线、荧光笔 |
|   白板：笔尖揭开线稿 |   3Blue1Brown：一个对象形变成下一个 |
|   Storytime：反应特写、笑点停顿 |   动态文字：主词砸进来 |
|   发布会：光斑底、毛玻璃卡、大数字 |   财经图表：先轴、后数据、只标一件事 |
---
## 能做什么
| 你说 | 它做 |
|---|---|
| 「复刻这个动画」「拆一下这段」 | 先跑拆解脚本量出转场、节拍网格、每段运动热图，再按机制用代码复刻 |
| 「做个梵高／莫奈／包豪斯那种的动画」 | 先设计一帧，再让它动起来；36张风格配方卡当起点 |
| 「用我的口播做一段艺术动画」 | 镜头表 → 定风格 → 世界画布加镜头 → 输出一条画面轨 |
| 「做一个人穿过一幅幅名画的片子」 | 长卷骨架：每个世界一个段文件，主角一路往右走，跨边界换画风，镜头只进不退 |
| 「做解说视频的动画段」 | 按口播选语法，喂一份 JSON，出一段时长精确到帧的片段（横竖屏、可透明底） |
| 「画面里要有人」 | 人交给生图模型出帧，代码负责合成、换帧和材质 |
| 「配个乐、卡节奏」 | BPM 网格、动机换乐器、结尾音效序列，纯代码合成 |
交付前有一道数字验收：`qa.py` 量稳定、效率、动感、流畅及文字框景

itens.descricao_en: Ears for coding agents: let AI hear, review and make sound. CPU-only, open source.
itens.readme:
# earshot
**Ears for coding agents.**
[**Watch the 0.4 launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) (35 s): its sound effects are
takes from the earshot bank placed with the launch kit, plus the one CC0 recording it shows being re-made, over a
licensed music track. Play every sound in the bank on
[the earshot site](https://leonxlnx.github.io/earshot-site/).
AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.
earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.
With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`), and
**translate a recording into code** it can vary (`earshot fit`). Both below.
**New in 0.4: the sound of a music-led launch film.** 51 new sounds made in code for the soft, short, mid-register
style those films use: rounded UI pops, wood and plastic knocks, short cut hits and sub hits with a kick, gated
glockenspiel / celesta / marimba notes and chime runs, water drops, camera shutters, reverse cymbals, a thump-whoosh,
short dark risers, bright swishes, burst glitches and mid dings (the bank now holds 252). A new `launch` kit preset
mixes every effect against the music bed instead of at a fixed level, says where each one sits against the cut (taps
lead it, whoosh peaks land after it) and how close a run may go. And `earshot fit` was re-made against professional
sound effects and measured on held-out clips ([below](#earshot-fit-audio-to-code)).
**New in 0.3: sound for code-made films.** A bank of sound effects stored as code that render by id in seconds,
with no models and no network: `earshot sfx` aims a whoosh, hit, click or note at a moment in the picture, and
`earshot kit` renders a whole film's effects with measured sync points ([below](#sound-for-films-bank-sfx-kits)).
```

itens.descricao_en: A tiny friend in your Mac's notch and on your iPhone that keeps an eye on your AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity and more. Approve from the notch or your Lock Screen.
itens.readme:
# Coucou
**A tiny friend that lives in your Mac's notch — or at the top of your screen on Windows and Linux — and keeps an eye on your AI coding agent sessions. And now on your phone too: iPhone and Android.**
Approve permissions, watch your agents work, drop a file, chat with Claude — all without leaving what you're doing. Walk away from your Mac and Mochi follows you to your iPhone: Lock Screen, Dynamic Island, widgets, Siri.
**New in 0.4: Coucou is a real Mac app.** Hold a key anywhere, speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, like Wispr Flow — free, open source, and offline with Parakeet. Record your calls without a bot in the meeting and get the transcript, the summary and the to-dos.
[ ](https://github.com/Louis-CFM/coucou/releases)
---
## Why
Some studios showed off gorgeous notch companions… and never let anyone use them.
**Coucou is the open version.** Every line of code is open source under the MIT License: read it, fork it, learn from it. The Coucou name, Mochi and the sounds stay © Louis Raillé (see [License](#license)).
Meet **Mochi**: a soft little squircle with big eyes that pops out of your notch, waves hello, follows your cursor with its eyes, gets annoyed when you poke it (and dizzy if you insist), and tells you the moment Claude Code needs you.
## Coucou on the Mac: dictation, notes, one window
Since 0.4, Coucou has its own window and sits in the Dock. On the left, **Flow** — everything about your voice — and **Notch**, all the settings of the island. *(macOS, GitHub build)*
- 🎙️ **Flow dictation** — hold a key anywhere on the Mac (right ⌥ by default, or fn, right ⌘ or right ⌃), speak, let go: your words are pasted where you type, in any app. Two quick taps for hands-free (or one, with a setting), Esc to cancel, ⌃⌘V to paste the last one again. Your clipboard gets back what it held.
- 💊 **The pill** — a small see-through pill at the bottom of the screen (or on its left or right edge). Hover it for a toolbar: dictate, record a call, open Coucou. While you speak, Mochi listens and nine dots follow your voice.
- 🦜 **Parakeet, offline** — run NVIDIA's Parakeet on your Mac's Neural Engine through [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio): more accurate, 25 languages, nothing leaves your Mac.
